extraction.name: CommonsenseQA
extraction.description: CommonsenseQA is a multiple-choice question answering dataset containing 12,247 questions designed to test commonsense knowledge. Questions are generated by crowd workers using subgraphs from ConceptNet, where a source concept and three semantically related target concepts prime workers to create questions requiring background knowledge. Each question is accompanied by five candidate answers, including one correct answer and four distractors.
extraction.creator: Alon Talmor (Tel-Aviv University; Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence); Jonathan Herzig (Tel-Aviv University); Nicholas Lourie (Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence); Jonathan Berant (Tel-Aviv University; Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence)
extraction.citeAs: Alon Talmor, Jonathan Herzig, Nicholas Lourie, and Jonathan Berant. 2019. CommonsenseQA: A Question Answering Challenge Targeting Commonsense Knowledge. arXiv:1811.00937v2 [cs.CL].
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions were collected by sampling subgraphs from ConceptNet (source concept plus three target concepts sharing the same relation), then having Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers author three multiple-choice questions per subgraph (one per target concept), add two additional distractors per question, and verify question quality. Web snippets were also collected by querying Google Search for each question-answer pair.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator; Web Scraping; Web API
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: 15% of formulated questions were filtered out during the quality verification process (questions not verified as answerable by at least one worker were excluded), reducing the total from 16,242 formulated questions to 12,247 final examples.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: ConceptNet knowledge base (version 5.5), providing concept nodes and commonsense relation edges used to construct question sets; Google Search web snippets retrieved for each question-answer pair (first 100 result snippets per candidate answer, yielding 500 snippets per question).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers generated and validated commonsense questions. Workers were shown a question concept and three answer concepts from ConceptNet and asked to formulate three questions (one per target concept), ensuring each question contains the question concept and has exactly one of the target concepts as the correct answer while the other two are not. Workers were instructed to avoid surface clues strongly related to the answer concept. Workers also added two additional distractors per question (one selected from ConceptNet, one authored manually). A separate disjoint group of workers verified question quality by annotating each question as unanswerable or choosing the correct answer; only questions verified correctly by at least one verifier were retained. A qualification threshold required that at least 75% of a worker's questions pass verification.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Each question was verified by 2 workers; only questions where at least one worker answered correctly were kept. This filtering process removed 15% of the questions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Questions often require background knowledge that is trivial to humans but is seldom explicitly reported on the web due to reporting bias; annotation artifacts and distributional biases in crowdsourced benchmarks are acknowledged as a general challenge for commonsense datasets
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: 10 workers formulated more than 85% of the questions, indicating high concentration among a small number of contributors; using web snippets as context does not lead to high performance, hinting that they do not carry a lot of useful information; BERT-large accuracy is expected to be roughly 75% assuming 100k examples, still substantially lower than human performance
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluation of commonsense question answering models; evaluating the degree of commonsense knowledge possessed by NLU systems; investigating question answering with prior knowledge; examining whether web text is useful for answering commonsense questions
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions were filtered through a quality verification process where a disjoint group of crowd workers verified each question; only questions verified by at least one worker who answered correctly were retained (filtering out 15% of questions). Two types of dataset splits were created: a random split and a question concept split, where each split ensures disjoint question concepts across training, development, and test sets. Hard distractors were added to each question: one selected from ConceptNet answer concepts sharing the same relation to the question concept, and one manually authored by workers, replacing random distractors to increase task difficulty.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Triplets were filtered by removing those with general or already well-explored relations, those where one concept exceeded four words or was not in English, and those where the edit distance between the two concepts was too low. Questions were verified by crowd workers and only those verified correctly by at least one of two workers were retained, filtering out 15% of questions.
